components.name: config
components.description: The program's settings, read from the environment and the command line, never from code.

decisions.question: Settings, name: type = default separated by commas - e.g. data_dir: str (required), log_level: str = "INFO" - or none?
decisions.answer: data_dir: str (required), log_level: str = "INFO"

decisions.question: Which settings are secrets (never logged, never printed), and where do they come from - e.g. smtp_password, from an environment variable - or none?
decisions.answer: None

components.name: logging_setup
components.description: Configures logging once, for the entry points (level from the config, one line per event, never a secret or personal data).

decisions.question: Where do the logs go and in which format - e.g. stderr, one line per event with time, level and message?
decisions.answer: stderr, one line per event: time, level, message

components.name: invoice
components.description: An invoice: number str, customer str, amount Decimal >= 0, status draft | sent | paid

decisions.question: Which fields are required, and which are optional (with which default) - e.g. number: str required, note: str = ""?
decisions.answer: All fields required

decisions.question: Which values are valid for each field (ranges, formats, lengths, allowed states) - e.g. amount >= 0 with 2 decimals, status draft, sent or paid?
decisions.answer: amount >= 0 with at most 2 decimals; status draft, sent or paid; number and customer not empty

decisions.question: Which fields must never appear in a log, an output or an error message (passwords, internal ids, personal data) - e.g. iban - or none?
decisions.answer: None

decisions.question: Is it changed after it is built, or frozen (a new one for every change) - e.g. frozen dataclass?
decisions.answer: Frozen: a change builds a new one (dataclasses.replace)

decisions.question: Which exit code does the command line give for it - e.g. InvoiceNotFound -> 3?
decisions.answer: Exit code 3

decisions.question: What does its message say - and never say (internal ids, personal data, secrets) - e.g. "Invoice not found", without the customer?
decisions.answer: A short fixed message, without personal data or secrets

components.name: invoices
components.description: Stores and finds invoices, one JSON file per invoice in the data folder

decisions.question: Where and in which format is the data kept - e.g. one JSON file per invoice in data/invoices/, or a SQLite table?
decisions.answer: One file NUMBER.json in data_dir, the fields of the invoice, amount as a string

decisions.question: Not found (e.g. get("F-42") when it does not exist): return None, or raise which domain error?
decisions.answer: Return None; the service raises the domain error

decisions.question: A crash while writing (e.g. the disk is full after half a file): how does a reader never see a half-written record - write to a temporary file then rename, or a transaction?
decisions.answer: Write to a temporary file next to it, then rename it

decisions.question: Two runs write the same record at the same moment: the last one wins, the second one is refused, or the second one waits (a lock)?
decisions.answer: The last one wins: marking paid twice gives the same file

P.retention.answer: 10 years (accounting law), then the file is deleted; one person's invoices are kept until then (legal obligation)

P.location.answer: The company's file server, in France

components.name: mark_paid
components.description: Find the invoice in the data folder, refuse a draft, mark it paid, save it, return it

decisions.question: What does it do, step by step (read, check, change, save, call) - e.g. read the invoice, check it is a draft, send it, mark it sent?
decisions.answer: Read the invoice; refuse a draft (ValueError); set status paid; save; return it

decisions.question: Something it needs does not exist: which domain error - e.g. InvoiceNotFound?
decisions.answer: InvoiceNotFoundError

decisions.question: Run twice with the same input (a retry, a re-run) - e.g. "send invoice F-42" twice: same result and no duplicate effect, or a domain error?
decisions.answer: The same result: an invoice already paid stays paid, saved again unchanged

decisions.question: What must be all or nothing, and what happens if a step fails in the middle - e.g. the e-mail is sent but marking it sent fails?
decisions.answer: Only one change, one save: nothing to undo

templates.name: archvow/fastapi-service
templates.description: FastAPI web service. Business rules live in a pure domain, the database and other services behind repositories and clients, each operation in a service, and HTTP only in the API layer.

questions.prompt: Language of the generated documents (README, AGENTS.md, guide, spec cards; archvow's commands stay English). One per project
Minimum Python version
Maximum line length (PEP 8 says 79; teams may agree on up to 99)
Where the code lives (decides CODEOWNERS and the branch rules that make the architects' approval binding)
What runs the checks and the tests (auto = the platform's own CI - GitLab CI or GitHub Actions; jenkins works with any platform)
Architects who approve guard changes (CODEOWNERS users or groups, e.g. @acme/architects)
questions.pattern_hint: one or more @user or @group/subgroup, separated by spaces

questions.prompt: Approved AI assistants, comma-separated (only these get instructions; others are flagged)
Approved AI reviewers, comma-separated (they read the change and write a report, never code; never the tool that wrote the code; empty = no AI review)
Analyse the code with SonarQube (sonar-project.properties, test reports, a scan step in the CI)

Let the approved AI assistants run the safe commands (archvow check/next/show, ruff, pytest, git status/diff/log...) and edit the code in src/ and tests/ without asking each time (no = they ask; the spec commands, the guard files, commits and pushes are never auto-approved)

How much the AI decides on its own (strict = every open question stops the code until a person answers; guided = the AI takes the suggested answer or proposes its own and goes on, a person reviews before the release; free = the AI decides and goes on, its choices are listed, never blocking)
Refuse to run inside an AI agent that is not in a sandbox (yes = an agent that can write outside the project is stopped; whatever you choose, an agent in YOLO mode is always stopped)
Rules archvow check applies (several, all or none); a few safety checks always run whatever you choose
Approved third-party packages besides fastapi, pydantic, uvicorn, httpx, pytest and hypothesis, comma-separated, as imported (e.g. sqlalchemy, jwt)
Folders holding the briefs the spec is drawn from with --from (user stories, functional specs, a Spec Kit `specs` folder), comma-separated (e.g. briefs,specs)
The most components this project may hold, foundations included (empty = no limit; past it, split the project) (e.g. 40)
questions.pattern_hint: a whole number, or empty for no limit

questions.prompt: The most lines of code under the package's folder - not blank, comments or docstrings; tests not counted (empty = no limit) (e.g. 8000)
questions.pattern_hint: a whole number, or empty for no limit

questions.prompt: Local checks before each commit (githooks = plain Git hook, no extra tool, no download)
Branch names (gitflow = feature/<ticket>-<short-name>, hotfix/<ticket>-<short-name>, release/<version>; none = free)

How this project's tickets are written, as a regular expression - branch names and `component add -s` must follow it (e.g. FATTRIB-[0-9]+ for FATTRIB-002, US-[0-9]+ for US-001; Enter = any Jira-style key)
questions.pattern_hint: a regular expression without quotes, spaces or slashes, such as [A-Z]+-[0-9]+

questions.prompt: Internal Python package index for CI (empty = public PyPI)
questions.pattern_hint: an http(s) URL such as https://nexus.acme.local/repository/pypi/simple, or empty

questions.prompt: Internal CI image with Python and git (empty = public python image)
questions.pattern_hint: an image reference such as registry.acme.local/data/python-spark:3.12, or empty

questions.prompt: FastAPI version line the project pins (upgrade deliberately; doctor checks it)
questions.pattern_hint: a FastAPI minor line such as 0.143

tool.description: One thing an agent may do - read or change data, call a system - with typed arguments the model fills and a docstring it reads.

retriever.description: Finds the passages a user may read that answer a question, best first, each with its source.

mcp_client.description: Gives the tools of one approved MCP server to the agents.

client.description: Talks to one other system (an HTTP API, a message broker, a source to index...).

router.description: Chooses the next step for a request, and the model role and thinking budget it gets.

node.description: One step of a graph - reads the state, calls a model or a tool, writes its result back.

agent.description: A model that chooses among its tools, step by step, until it has an answer (LangChain's create_agent).

graph.description: The workflow - its steps and how they follow each other, compiled with the memory.

api.description: The HTTP API - signs the user in, builds the access scope, runs the graph. Run with uvicorn --factory.

mcp_server.description: Serves tools to other assistants over MCP (the company's assistants, IDEs).

index_job.description: Copies one source into the index - Documents, chunks, embeddings - only what changed.

templates.name: archvow/pyspark-pipeline
templates.description: Batch PySpark pipeline. Pure, lazy DataFrame transformations are isolated from I/O, sessions and orchestration so each piece is testable on its own.

questions.prompt: Language of the generated documents (README, AGENTS.md, guide, spec cards; archvow's commands stay English). One per project
Minimum Python version
Maximum line length (PEP 8 says 79; teams may agree on up to 99)
Where the code lives (decides CODEOWNERS and the branch rules that make the architects' approval binding)
What runs the checks and the tests (auto = the platform's own CI - GitLab CI or GitHub Actions; jenkins works with any platform)
Architects who approve guard changes (CODEOWNERS users or groups, e.g. @acme/architects)
questions.pattern_hint: one or more @user or @group/subgroup, separated by spaces

questions.prompt: Approved AI assistants, comma-separated (only these get instructions; others are flagged)
Approved AI reviewers, comma-separated (they read the change and write a report, never code; never the tool that wrote the code; empty = no AI review)
Analyse the code with SonarQube (sonar-project.properties, test reports, a scan step in the CI)

Let the approved AI assistants run the safe commands (archvow check/next/show, ruff, pytest, git status/diff/log...) and edit the code in src/ and tests/ without asking each time (no = they ask; the spec commands, the guard files, commits and pushes are never auto-approved)

How much the AI decides on its own (strict = every open question stops the code until a person answers; guided = the AI takes the suggested answer or proposes its own and goes on, a person reviews before the release; free = the AI decides and goes on, its choices are listed, never blocking)
Refuse to run inside an AI agent that is not in a sandbox (yes = an agent that can write outside the project is stopped; whatever you choose, an agent in YOLO mode is always stopped)
Rules archvow check applies (several, all or none); a few safety checks always run whatever you choose
Approved third-party packages besides pyspark, pytest and hypothesis, comma-separated, as imported (e.g. yaml, requests)
Folders holding the briefs the spec is drawn from with --from (user stories, functional specs, a Spec Kit `specs` folder), comma-separated (e.g. briefs,specs)
The most components this project may hold, foundations included (empty = no limit; past it, split the project) (e.g. 40)
questions.pattern_hint: a whole number, or empty for no limit

questions.prompt: The most lines of code under the package's folder - not blank, comments or docstrings; tests not counted (empty = no limit) (e.g. 8000)
questions.pattern_hint: a whole number, or empty for no limit

questions.prompt: Local checks before each commit (githooks = plain Git hook, no extra tool, no download)
Branch names (gitflow = feature/<ticket>-<short-name>, hotfix/<ticket>-<short-name>, release/<version>; none = free)

How this project's tickets are written, as a regular expression - branch names and `component add -s` must follow it (e.g. FATTRIB-[0-9]+ for FATTRIB-002, US-[0-9]+ for US-001; Enter = any Jira-style key)
questions.pattern_hint: a regular expression without quotes, spaces or slashes, such as [A-Z]+-[0-9]+

questions.prompt: Internal Python package index for CI (empty = public PyPI)
questions.pattern_hint: an http(s) URL such as https://nexus.acme.local/repository/pypi/simple, or empty

questions.prompt: Internal CI image with Python and git (and Java 17 for Spark) (empty = public python image)
questions.pattern_hint: an image reference such as registry.acme.local/data/python-spark:3.12, or empty

Scheduler that runs the pipeline (none = run entrypoint.sh yourself or from your own scheduler)

layers.name: p0_common
layers.description: Shared foundations - SparkSession factory, configuration, constants

layers.name: p1_domain
layers.description: Schemas and pure, lazy DataFrame -> DataFrame transformations

layers.name: p2_io
layers.description: Readers and writers - the only place that touches storage

layers.name: p3_jobs
layers.description: Jobs wiring readers, transformations and writers together

layers.name: p4_entrypoints
layers.description: Process entry points (CLI, scheduler, Databricks/EMR job)

utility.description: Shared helper or constants module (no Spark actions, no I/O).

schema.description: Explicit StructType contract for a dataset.

reader.description: Reads one dataset and enforces its schema.

kinds.name: files
kinds.description: Reads one dataset and enforces its schema.

kinds.name: table
kinds.description: Reads one table of the catalog (Hive metastore, Unity, Glue; Delta, Iceberg or Hudi) and enforces its schema.

kinds.name: jdbc
kinds.description: Reads a table or a query of a database over JDBC (spark.read.jdbc) and enforces its schema.

kinds.name: connector
kinds.description: Reads with a Spark connector (spark.read.format(...)) - BigQuery, Snowflake, Redshift, Synapse, MongoDB, Cassandra, Elasticsearch, Kafka read in batch... - and enforces its schema.

kinds.name: custom
kinds.description: Reads a source Spark has no reader for (a REST API, SFTP, a SaaS export, an in-house file format) with its own Python code - a Python data source (Spark 4.0) or calls on the executors - and enforces its schema.

kinds.name: table
kinds.description: Writes one table of the catalog (Hive metastore, Unity, Glue; Delta, Iceberg or Hudi).

kinds.name: jdbc
kinds.description: Writes a table of a database over JDBC (df.write.jdbc).

kinds.name: connector
kinds.description: Writes with a Spark connector (df.write.format(...)) - BigQuery, Snowflake, Redshift, Synapse, MongoDB, Cassandra, Elasticsearch, Kafka...

kinds.name: custom
kinds.description: Writes to a target Spark has no writer for (a REST API, SFTP, a SaaS import, an in-house format) with its own Python code - foreachPartition, or a Python data source writer (Spark 4.0).

job.description: Orchestrates read -> transform -> write for one output.

entrypoint.description: Process entry point that parses arguments and runs one job.

templates.name: archvow/python-app
templates.description: Python application or library, no framework imposed. Business rules live in a pure domain, files, databases and other services behind repositories and clients, each operation in a service, the command line in an entry point. src layout, pyproject.toml, ruff, pytest, mypy.

layers.name: p0_common
layers.description: Shared foundations - settings, logging, small helpers every layer may use

layers.name: p1_domain
layers.description: Business rules - data classes, domain errors and pure functions, no I/O

layers.name: p2_io
layers.description: Repositories and clients - the only place that reads and writes files, databases and other services

layers.name: p3_services
layers.description: Services - one operation each, calling repositories and clients and applying the domain's rules

layers.name: p4_entrypoints
layers.description: Entry points - the command line, which parses arguments, calls a service and sets the exit code

utility.description: A small helper every layer may use (no business rule, no I/O beyond what it says).

model.description: A data class - the shape and the validation of one kind of data.

error.description: A domain error - raised by the domain and the services, turned into a message and an exit code by the entry point.

logic.description: A pure business rule - a function of its inputs, no I/O.

repository.description: Stores and finds one kind of data (files, a database).

client.description: Talks to one other system (an HTTP API, a mail server, a message broker...).

service.description: One operation - calls repositories and clients and applies the domain's rules.

cli.description: The command line - parses the arguments, calls a service, prints the result, sets the exit code.

regimes.name: GDPR
regimes.title: Personal data (GDPR / RGPD): purpose, legal basis, retention, location, recipients

rules.GDPR002: Personal data processed without a decided purpose and legal basis
rules.GDPR003: Personal data written without a decided retention and erasure
rules.GDPR008: Personal data stored or sent without a decided location, recipient and transfer safeguard

regimes.name: GLBA
regimes.title: GLBA (US financial institutions): nonpublic personal information shared only after notice and opt-out, encrypted, limited, disposed of, incidents reported
regimes.law: Gramm-Leach-Bliley Act, Title V: the Privacy Rule (Regulation P, 12 CFR 1016); the Interagency Guidelines Establishing Information Security Standards and the Computer-Security Incident Notification Rule (banks); the FTC Safeguards Rule (16 CFR 314, other financial institutions)

rules.GLBA001: Nonpublic personal information shared without a decided notice and opt-out
rules.GLBA002: Nonpublic personal information without decided access limits
rules.GLBA003: Nonpublic personal information stored without decided encryption at rest and in transit
rules.GLBA004: Nonpublic personal information stored without decided secure disposal
rules.GLBA005: Nonpublic personal information stored without a decided way to detect and report incidents
rules.GLBA006: Nonpublic personal information sent to a service provider without decided oversight

regimes.name: US-PRIVACY
regimes.title: US state privacy laws (CCPA/CPRA and the other state laws, strictest common rule): notice, opt-outs, sensitive data, requests, assessments, minors
regimes.law: California Consumer Privacy Act as amended by the CPRA and its regulations (11 CCR 7000 ff.), and the other state comprehensive privacy laws; COPPA (16 CFR 312) for children under 13

rules.USP001: Personal information collected without a decided notice at collection
rules.USP002: Sale, sharing or profiling not decided, or without an opt-out that honours universal signals
rules.USP003: Sensitive personal information used without decided consent and limits
rules.USP004: Data of minors used without decided age checks and parental consent
rules.USP005: High-risk processing without a decided risk assessment (or automated decision without notice and opt-out)
rules.USP006: Personal information stored without a decided way for consumer requests to reach it
rules.USP007: Personal information stored without a decided retention per category
rules.USP008: Personal information sent to a third party without a decided contract and opt-out check
